data.name: Lysandros
data.gender_notes: Lysandros is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'lysos' meaning 'loose' or 'free', and 'andros' meaning 'man' or 'warrior'. In ancient Greece, this name was given to those who were liberated from slavery. In Christian tradition, it is believed to represent a free man in Christ, liberated from the bondage of sin. The name Lysandros carries the meaning “Liberator, Free Man” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Lysandros usually hope their child will grow to embody liberator, free man and live with faith, good character and purpose.

It is believed to embody the essence of a believer who has been liberated from the bondage of sin and embraced the boundless freedom offered by Christ. This interpretation resonates strongly with modern-day believers, who recognize the transformative power of faith in overcoming the burdens of life. Thus, when bestowed upon a child, Lysandros is not only a badge of honor reflecting an ancient legacy but also a pious reminder of the spiritual journey toward enlightenment and redemption.
